name: Asterid Queen

spells.name: Falling Stars
spells.text:
Area 4 40-foot bursts

---

You reach into the skies and call down an array of falling stars that explode upon colliding with the ground. Choose for the falling stars to be airbursts (sonic), asteroids (fire), comets (cold), or plasma (electricity). The spell gains the trait of the falling star type you chose. The four stars' central 10-foot bursts can't overlap. Each falling star deals 6d10 bludgeoning damage to each creature in the 10-foot burst at the center of its area of effect before exploding, dealing 14d6 energy damage of the type you chose to each creature in its 40-foot burst. A creature in any of the areas attempts one basic Reflex save against the spell no matter how many overlapping explosions it's caught in and can take each type of damage only once.

---

Heightened (+1) The bludgeoning damage increases by 1d10, and the energy damage increases by 2d6.

spells.name: Foresight
spells.text:
You gain a sixth sense that warns you of danger that might befall the target of the spell. If you choose a creature other than yourself as the target, you create a psychic link through which you can inform the target of danger. This link is a mental effect. Due to the amount of information this spell requires you to process, you can't have more than one foresight spell in effect at a time. Casting foresight again ends the previous foresight. While foresight is in effect, the target gains a +2 status bonus to initiative rolls and isn't Off-Guard against Undetected creatures or when flanked. In addition, you gain the following reaction: Foresight

Spell Effect: Foresight

spells.name: Eclipse Burst
spells.text:
A globe of freezing darkness explodes in the area, dealing 8d10 cold damage to creatures in the area, plus an additional 8d4 void damage to living creatures. Each creature in the area must attempt a Reflex save.

If the globe overlaps with an area of magical light or affects a creature affected by magical light, eclipse burst attempts to counteract the light effect.

---
Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature takes half damage.

Failure The creature takes full damage.

Critical Failure The creature takes double damage and becomes Blinded by the darkness for an unlimited duration.

---
Heightened (+1) The cold damage increases by 1d10 and the void damage against the living increases by 1d4.

spells.name: Blanket of Stars
spells.text:
A flowing cloak of utter darkness drapes over you, filled with pinpricks of light like distant stars. It imparts the stillness of the cosmos to you, granting you a +2 status bonus to Stealth checks to Hide and Sneak.

While outside under a starry night sky, you're also Invisible as long as you remain still. When moving under a starry night sky, you're Concealed instead.

Gazing too closely into the stars is disorienting. Any creature that ends its turn adjacent to you must attempt a Will save; this is a mental, visual effect.

---
Success The creature is unaffected.

Failure The creature is Dazzled until the end of its next turn.

Critical Failure The creature is Confused and dazzled until the end of its next turn.

items.name: (Nymph Queen) Tied to the Land
items.text:
An asterid queen is intrinsically tied to a vast, remote location with a clear view of the night sky, such as an isolated island or island chain, a mountain range, or an open plain far from the light pollution of civilization.

---
A nymph queen is intrinsically tied to a specific region. As long as the queen is healthy, the environment is exceptionally resilient, allowing the nymph queen to automatically attempt to counteract any spell that would harm the environment (such as the Blight ritual), using her spell DC with a counteract rank equal to the highest-rank druid spell she can cast.

When the nymph queen becomes physically or psychologically unhealthy, however, her warded region eventually becomes twisted or unhealthy as well. In that case, restoring the nymph queen swiftly heals the entire region.

items.name: (Nymph Queen) Nymph's Beauty
items.text: 30 feet. A creature who starts their turn in the aura must succeed at a DC 37 Will save save or become Stunned 1.

items.name: (Nymph Queen) Change Shape
items.text:
Nymph queens can transform between their original form, which looks much like a typical nymph of their kind, and any Small or Medium humanoid form, typically choosing a more humanoid-looking version of their natural form.

---

items.name: (Nymph Queen) Focus Beauty
items.text:
Requirements The target creature is affected by the asterid queen's nymph's beauty aura

---
Effect The target falls to its knees and is stunned for 1 hour.

items.name: Court of Night
items.text: The asterid queen opens an entrance to an extradimensional living space Concealed within the shadows of the land to which she is bound. She can bring up to eight adjacent, willing creatures with her. This space can only be entered or exited at night, and only by the queen's will.

items.name: Crown of Stars
items.text: An asterid queen wears a brilliantly shining crown of stars that increases the effect of their natural starshine to 15 feet of bright light and 15 feet of dim light beyond that. The asterid queen can choose to remove her crown with a single Interact action, reducing the effect to that of starshine (as asterid) until the crown is returned to her head.

items.name: Knowledge from the Stars
items.text: Effect The asterid queen looks to the stars for guidance and rolls a d20. Until the start of their next turn, they can use the result of their roll in place of making a check or saving throw. The asterid can't use Knowledge from the Stars again for 1 hour.

items.name: Starbeam
items.text: Effect The asterid launches a beam of starlight in a 120-foot line. Creatures in the line take 9d6 fire damage (DC 40 basic Reflex save save). Creatures who fail their save also become Dazzled for 1 round.

text:
Asterid queens reign over entire constellations and clusters of stars reflected in the seas. In practice, they rule mountain ranges, vast swaths of tundra at the Crown of the World, and remote islands far out to sea where the nights are long and dark. Their domains often (though not always) overlap with those of other nymph queens who sheltered the asterid when she was younger and still accumulating power. Asterid queens always remember their friends and return the favors owed with both powerful magic and the divinatory guidance of the stars.

---
Asterids are nymphs of the stars, serene guardians of clear night skies and isolated pockets of the natural world far from the smog and light pollution of mortal cities. They spend their nights sitting in open fields or standing at the crests of high mountains, their heads tilted back to silently watch the stars go by. The rapturous, dreamy expressions asterids wear during their nightly observations have inspired countless works of art on the themes of beauty and longing.

As asterids are bound to general locations rather than specific natural features, they often must rely on alliances and friendships with other kinds of nymphs to find shelter. During the day, asterids generally end up sleeping in the tree-homes of dryads, beneath naiad ponds, or in the courts of their queens. This, alongside the asterids' generally quiet and gentle demeanor, leads many other nymphs to be somewhat protective of them, especially the asterid queens.

Mortals looking to establish an observatory can ask for no better location than one beloved by an asterid, though they would do well to approach such an endeavor with care and diplomacy. Those who come to the nymph with deference and respect the sanctity of the surrounding natural beauty may earn themselves a quiet but attentive guardian, eager to share their knowledge in exchange for the ability to more closely observe their beloved stars. Those who mar the natural world with excess construction or, worst of all, drown out the stars with excess light provoke the asterid's wrath and find their endeavor cursed with misfortune, if not destroyed entirely by the fury of the nymph's protective friends.
